title: Leaving Chicago in 1938: Detroit and Cincinnati
summary: On tour out of Chicago Roy recalls a debt dispute in Detroit and driving fast to the Cotton Club in Cincinnati.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Doing his scales. So when you left Chicago, you went out on the road with the band...
Yeah.
And how long did that keep up? Did you come to New
Eldridge - 103
York with the band then?

Well, we were on our way to New York. This was in '38, I guess. Because we played little dates. We played Detroit at a theatre there. I had a very funny incident there. I played at this theatre. And I knew the name of that theatre; I can't think of it now....
Oh yeah, I know what you mean, because we tried to look for it when they had us in Detroit last year.
Did you see it? Or was it torn down?
We couldn't find it.
It was right across from the Detroit Hotel. I think I told you about that, though, didn't I?
What, that incident?
Yeah.
I don't think so.
Well, we played there, and I'm trying to think where in the hell did we stay there...? Mmm, I can't remember where we stayed there. Well, anyhow, I know this theatre we played.

Anyhow, I had a friend there that was kind of with people who could lean on you about money and things that you owed people. And at the end of the day, the cat started getting a little strange about my money, you know. So I went over, and asked my friend would he come over and speak
Eldridge - 104

to him. And he got dressed and come over there, and the man hurried up and got our money together. But we were not so (?) when we played... Oh, I know where we went. We played the Cotton Club, I'm trying to think, in Cincinnati, but Zutty was with me when we played there. So that must have been before Harold...
Maybe you did a little tour out of Chicago, and then you came back.
Yeah. We played the Cotton Club. Because I remember we was driving so fast... Zutty had his car, we were going about 90, right close behind each other, you know. Dogs had their heads out the windows.
But things was pretty rough then, too, because Vi had a lot of pennies, and she put them together and she'd cook a pot of beans and shit like that. Heh-heh.
